tier_reason: First-party benchmark in the same organisation's MRPT/gtsam2mrpt_serial repo (code public at tests/main.cpp, testSerializeProfiler, CPU i7-6700HQ stated) but compiler, flags and build type are not stated anywhere, so it cannot reach A; results exist only as two log-scale PNG plots committed 2022-04-19.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README of MRPT/gtsam2mrpt_serial claims 'approximately 2x faster serialization and deserialization for mid-sized factor graphs'. Its own plots (docs/profiling-ser.png, docs/profiling-deser.png; bars read approximately from a log axis, derived from page data) show serialization about 1.7-2.2x faster for 56 to 22001 factors (about 3.7x at 12 factors), but deserialization only about 1.0-1.2x from 276 to 22001 factors (parity at 1101 factors), about 1.5x at 56 and about 2.7x at 12. The 2x deserialization claim for mid-sized graphs is overstated.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark is in a separate repo (MRPT/gtsam2mrpt_serial, same organisation, first-party) and measures a GTSAM bridge built on mrpt-serialization, not the core library on generic data; the baseline is Boost.Serialization through GTSAM, not protobuf, FlatBuffers or another widely used serializer. Deserialization is roughly at parity with Boost for mid-sized graphs despite the README's 2x claim; only serialization is about 2x. Harness asymmetry: gtsam::serializeToBinaryStream / deserializeFromBinaryStream construct a boost binary_oarchive/iarchive inside the timed region (twice per rep, for Values and graph), while the MRPT archive is constructed before the CTimeLoggerEntry starts, which inflates the small-graph ratios. The plots are stale: committed 2022-04-19 with MRPT 2.4.4, and their factor counts (12, 56, 276, 1101, 5501, 22001 = 11N+1) do not match the current tests/sampleData.cpp generator (12N+1 factors, robust noise models added since), so the published numbers were not produced by the current code; the repo now requires MRPT 3.0. Compiler, flags and build type are unstated; exact timings exist only as images. The profiling code only compiles when GTSAM uses Boost (GTSAM 4.2), uses mrpt::system::CTimeLogger with max(5, 1000/N) repetitions, and runs into in-memory streams (CMemoryStream vs std::stringstream).

notes: README quotes match the page, but reading the deserialization plot shows near parity (about 1.0-1.2x) for 276-22001 factors, so the claim is overstated; tier stays C. The measured artifact is MRPT/gtsam2mrpt_serial (7 stars, BSD-3-Clause), not mrpt/mrpt core; consider a repo_url override or naming the entry gtsam2mrpt_serial. Metadata checked: mrpt/mrpt 2.2k stars, BSD-3-Clause, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-10-06.

tier_reason: First-party README Table 1 with flags stated in Appendix A, but no benchmark script, no compiler named, no CPU model (only 'dual core x86_64'), and no package versions, so C.

corrections.caveats: The claim is build time and footprint, not runtime curses performance; no runtime benchmark against ncurses was found. Single run, no repeats or variance, ncurses and netbsd-curses versions not stated, and the table dates from the 2016-era README (README history from March 2016; no later commit touches the table), so it reflects ncurses of about ten years ago. The configure-heavy ncurses build is single-threaded for part of its time (the README says netbsd curses should scale better with more jobs, which is untested). The installed-size row is not like for like: Appendix A says netbsd curses was installed without manpages (ncurses: 1.1 MB) and without the terminfo database (ncurses: 6.4 MB), so excluding those the gap is about 8.4 MB vs 1.3 MB (derived from page data), not 15.9 MB vs 1.3 MB. Binary sizes are from a size-optimised (-Os, gc-sections, stripped) build. Not a 100% drop-in replacement: mouse handling is no-op macros, some functions (vidputs) are missing, only 510 color pairs, and programs touching ncurses struct members need patches. First-party numbers, no benchmark script in the repo.

notes: All Table 1 numbers match the README (59 s vs 9 s make -j2, 6.6x derived; 15.9 MB vs 1.3 MB installed; 346 KB vs 150 KB shared lib; 334 KB vs 288 KB static nano). Installed-size row excludes manpages and terminfo db for netbsd curses only.
